Quran Grid

Every square is one of the Quran's 77,429 words, read from the top right like an Arabic page. Pick a trend to see a pattern in the text and why it matters, or search for any word.

    month
    Words whose English meaning is “month” (month* also finds months)
    شمس
    Arabic: a root if it is one, otherwise a spelling
    root:رحم
    Every word built on a root
    tr:"sacred month"
    Verses whose English translation has this phrase
    surah:2 · juz:30
    Only look in a surah or juz (ranges work too: surah:1-10)
    type:meccan
    Only Meccan (or Medinan) surahs
    length:50-200
    Verses of 50 to 200 words
    ar:*ون
    Words ending in ون (ar:ال* starts with, ar:=كتاب exact word)
    2:255
    One verse, or a range like 2:255-257

    Combine terms: a space means AND, | means OR, commas list choices (root:شمس,قمر) and a minus leaves things out (-type:medinan). For grammar there are also lemma:, tag: (PN names, VOC “O …”, INL opening letters), pos: (N, V, P), at:last (last word of each verse) and has:"root:قمر" (verses containing such a word).

      How it works

      The text is split into words as the Quranic Arabic Corpus splits it: 77,429 words in 6,236 verses, laid out on the smallest near-square grid (279 × 278 for words, 79 × 79 for verses, 25 × 25 for the 604 pages). Each trend is a saved search. Most come from analysing the text directly; popular claims are included only where the count holds. Every count is re-run when the page is built.

      “Earliest”, “middle” and “last” mean thirds of the surahs in the traditional revelation order, which early scholars reconstructed and which is not certain. Meccan and Medinan labels apply to whole surahs. Searching ignores vowel marks and treats letter variants such as أ إ آ as ا.
